newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Congress chief ordered to reply to complaint.
newsitem.headline: Indian Congress chief ordered to reply to complaint.

text.p: An Indian court on Friday ordered Congress party president Sitaram Kesri to respond to a public interest complaint alleging that as party treasurer he had received illegal foreign contributions, lawyers said.

The two-judge Delhi High Court bench directed Kesri, the Home (Interior) Ministry and the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) to respond by May 20, showing cause why the legal petition should not be admitted, they said.
"We'll reply to the notice and fight the case legally," Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told Reuters by telephone from the western city of Pune.

The petition, filed by a free-lance journalist, said that Kesri accepted a total of 30 million rupees ($840,000) in the form of three cheques from Germany in violation of the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA), local news agencies said.
Indian political parties are barred from receiving money from foreign sources. FCRA offences are punishable by up to five years in jail, news agencies said.

Kesri was party treasurer from 1979 until he was elevated to president last September when his predecessor, former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, stepped down after being implicated in three corruption cases. Rao has said he is innocent.
Kesri, who provoked the downfall of former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda this month by withdrawing his party's vital backing, could not be reached for comment.
United News of India (UNI) said the foreign contributions came to light during a recent audit of the Congress party's accounts for the years 1993 to 1995.
Earlier this month, Delhi tax authorities said Congress had failed to file satisfactory income tax accounts for the 1994/95 (April-March) year in time and lost its right to an exemption.

The chief commissioner of income tax in Delhi said at the time that Congress had been told to pay about 250 million rupees ($7 million) in tax for the year ended on March 31, 1995, because it failed to file proper accounts by the end of March.
Ordinarily political parties are exempt from paying tax.
UNI said counsel for the CBDT told the court on Friday that the department had taken into account the foreign contribution when ordering Congress to pay taxes for 1994/95.
The complaint accused the Home (Interior) Ministry of failing to take action against Kesri or Congress over the alleged FCRA violation, a government lawyer said.

"I pointed out as a preliminary objection that the petition is based entirely on newspaper reports and that it carried an affidavit giving no details for the basis of the allegations," additional solicitor general A.M. Singhvi told Reuters. "In addition, the petition appeared to be motivated."
The two-judge panel will hold a hearing on May 20 and then decide whether to admit the petition, Singhvi said. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
